key_points: Original HADDOCK is information-driven docking using ambiguous interaction restraints (AIRs)
Biochemical/biophysical data such as NMR chemical shift perturbations or mutagenesis data can define interface restraints
Best-ranked structures by intermolecular energies were closest to native structures in the reported examples
HADDOCK2.0 expanded to proteins, nucleic acids, oligosaccharides, ligands, and multicomponent systems
Protocol improvements include solvated docking and automatic semirigid/flexible treatment
Scoring and flexibility handling are major docking challenges assessed in CAPRI
HADDOCK2.2 emphasizes user-friendly integrative modeling of biomolecular complexes
Accuracy improves by incorporating experimental or predictive information into docking
Portal supports mixed molecule types and additional restraints
Recent HADDOCK application to protein-glycan interactions highlights modularity beyond protein-protein docking
Success depends strongly on binding-site knowledge and partner flexibility
Benchmarking reports top-5 success rates for bound and unbound settings

contract_updates: Position present work as validation-oriented structural analysis, not a full HADDOCK rerun
